items.why: Teams relying on automatic metrics for romanized Indic outputs may overestimate quality, so human or specialized evaluation is needed.

items.title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses
items.summary: Researchers show routine operations can break architectural pattern relationships in LLM agent harnesses without any code change, studying five harnesses and their plugins.
items.why: Routine runtime changes silently altering guardrail and state patterns could undermine safety in production agent systems.

items.title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering
items.summary: Researchers propose AdaAlloc, which adaptively allocates a fixed visual-token budget between global context and local detail for long-video question answering.
items.why: Adaptive token budgeting could improve long-video QA accuracy under the fixed context limits engineers face in multimodal LLM deployments.

items.title: AlienBench: A Benchmark of Structural Novelty in Language Model Outputs
items.summary: Researchers introduce AlienBench, a benchmark for measuring how structurally novel language model outputs are relative to familiar examples.
items.why: Gives engineers a fixed reference for evaluating creativity claims instead of relying on subjective human or LLM-judge novelty ratings.

items.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
items.summary: Researchers present SPDMX, an openly licensed multitrack stem audio dataset created by rendering public-domain PDMX symbolic music scores.
items.why: Offers a freely redistributable source of individual music stems for training, avoiding copyright limits on training audio.

items.title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
items.summary: A paper proposes a spike-based neuromorphic framework for condition monitoring in power electronics using only three-phase AC current measurements.

items.title: Learning Generative Dynamics for 3D Molecule Generation via Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constraints
items.summary: Researchers propose SensDiff, a diffusion framework that integrates symbolic chemical rules into 3D molecule generation to improve chemical validity.
items.why: Shows a method for enforcing domain rules inside generative models, relevant to teams building constrained scientific generation.

items.title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose FIND, a test-time adaptation method that uses frequency-domain invariance to improve LiDAR 3D object detection under domain shift.

items.title: SIFR: Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement
items.summary: Researchers introduce SIFR, a reward fine-tuning method for flow models that uses signed advantages to suppress low-reward samples and improve training stability.
items.why: Addresses mode collapse in iterative reward fine-tuning of flow models, a practical issue for teams doing generative model post-training.

items.title: RPEG: Training Reasoning Language Models Scalably and Cost-Effectively
items.summary: Researchers present RPEG, a data-centric graph representation that jointly optimizes structure and execution to make reinforcement learning training of reasoning models cheaper and more scalable.
items.why: Targets the cost and complexity of multi-model RL pipelines, which matters for teams training reasoning models at scale.

items.title: On the Limits of Execution Traces for Repairing Assertion Failures in LLM-Generated Code
items.summary: Researchers argue that assertion failures carry little fault-location information and propose Breakpoint Debugging, which annotates failed programs with runtime variable values for LLM repair.
items.why: Suggests richer runtime feedback may improve automated repair of LLM-generated code beyond raw assertion error messages.

items.title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
items.summary: Researchers introduce PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running software performance optimization, and study whether agents can recursively improve their harnesses using task experience.
items.why: Highlights that agent harnesses optimized offline may miss difficulties that emerge in long, open-ended runs.

items.title: HMMF-Net: A Lightweight Hierarchical Multi-Frame Multimodal Fusion Network for Accurate Fish Feeding Intensity Assessment
items.summary: Researchers propose HMMF-Net, a lightweight multimodal network fusing multi-frame video and acoustic signals to assess fish feeding intensity on edge devices.

items.title: FondueQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating Parametric Compensation in Multi-Hop QA
items.summary: Researchers introduce FondueQA, a multi-hop question answering benchmark designed to separate parametric knowledge from benchmark contamination when evaluating LLMs.
items.why: Offers a way to assess model knowledge without confounding from memorized public benchmark data.

items.title: AudioSphere: Towards Self-Supervised Spatial Audio Representation Models
items.summary: Researchers propose AudioSphere, a self-supervised model that learns spatial audio representations usable for frame-level tasks like sound event detection and localization.

items.title: Diversity-Aware Client Selection for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
items.summary: Researchers study diversity-aware client selection to reduce communication overhead in federated learning under non-IID data distributions.

items.title: A Stochastic Latent Variable Generalization of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
items.summary: Researchers present S-JEPA, a stochastic latent variable extension of joint-embedding predictive architectures for masked image prediction.

items.title: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training
items.summary: Researchers propose training prototype-based classifiers with Lipschitz constraints to improve robustness while keeping interpretability and closed-form certification.
items.why: Offers interpretable classifiers with certifiable robustness bounds, relevant where explainability and adversarial robustness both matter.

items.title: Syn2DRE: Synergistic Dual Teacher-Student Framework for Document-level Relation Extraction
items.summary: Syn2DRE is a semi-supervised dual teacher-student framework that combines self-supervised learning with cross-supervision to produce more reliable pseudo-labels for document-level relation extraction.
items.why: It targets reducing costly annotation needs for relation extraction by improving pseudo-label quality and limiting confirmation bias.

items.title: Reliable Prerequisite-Aware Learning Path Recommendation under Uncertain Knowledge Structures: Long-Horizon Evaluation and Cross-Dataset Validation
items.summary: Researchers propose a reliability-oriented, prerequisite-aware framework for learning-path recommendation that tests robustness under uncertain knowledge structures and long-horizon path generation.
items.why: It highlights that high next-item accuracy does not guarantee reliable long-horizon recommendation behavior, a useful evaluation lesson for recommender builders.

items.title: When Feedback Becomes a Backdoor: Tracing Backdoor Skill Formation in Text-Space Skill Optimization
items.summary: A paper shows that poisoning reference answers in text-space skill optimization can implant a persistent trigger-conditioned rule in agent Skills without access to the model or optimizer.
items.why: Agent skill files refined from feedback can carry backdoors, so teams using automated skill optimization need to treat feedback data as an attack surface.

items.title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes
items.summary: HiMEM proposes hippocampus-inspired memory consolidation, pruning, and composition for vision-language-action robot models operating in 3D scenes.
items.why: It addresses memory noise in VLA models that hinders cross-task transfer, relevant to teams building long-horizon robot agents.

items.title: Mitigating Covariate Shift in Behavioral Cloning via Robust Stationary Distribution Correction
items.summary: A paper proposes a robust stationary distribution correction method to mitigate covariate shift in behavioral cloning for offline imitation learning.
items.why: Covariate shift is a known failure mode of behavioral cloning, so a more robust correction could matter for teams training policies from offline demonstrations.

items.title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
items.summary: Researchers report that a language model can repair a robot policy's instruction grounding by editing 65 token-embedding rows, raising held-out paraphrase success from 86.3% to 92.0% in the best run.
items.why: It suggests weight-space edits can fix robot instruction-following without retraining or new demonstrations, though gains are measured on one policy.

items.title: SPSC: Zero-Shot Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Semantic Preservation and Subspace Calibration
items.summary: SPSC introduces a method for zero-shot cross-subject EEG-to-image reconstruction using semantic preservation and subspace calibration.

items.title: Artificial Shoppers and Attention Competition
items.summary: An economics paper studies how AI shopping assistants and delegated AI agents affect price competition, platform profit, and consumer welfare across product comparison modes.
items.why: It frames how AI shopping agents could reshape marketplace pricing and platform incentives, relevant to teams building commerce agents.

items.title: DataHelix: A CPU-GPU Co-Scheduling Data Plane for Multimodal Model Training
items.summary: DataHelix presents a CPU-GPU co-scheduling data plane to handle heterogeneous preprocessing and compute times across data-parallel ranks in multimodal model training.
items.why: Per-sample variation in decode and compute cost can stall synchronous training, so co-scheduling data loading with GPU work addresses a real throughput bottleneck.

items.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
items.summary: SmartBloch-Agent is an agentic framework that aims to automate MRI pulse sequence design and optimization from imaging objectives to executable protocols.

items.title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning
items.summary: DexDICE introduces dual-expert offline imitation learning that combines safety-compliant and high-performing demonstrations to balance safety guarantees with returns.
items.why: It offers a way to meet safety constraints in offline imitation learning without hand-designed cost functions or costly safe, high-performing demonstrations.

items.title: Logit Laundering: Evading Data-Use Auditing in Large Language Models
items.summary: A paper studies how non-compliant LLM providers could evade watermarking-based data-use auditing, showing adversarial weaknesses in current detection methods.
items.why: Teams relying on watermarks to prove unauthorized training data use should account for adversarial evasion in their audit assumptions.

items.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: RCEA proposes a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates policy entropy by reward outcome to better explain exploration and reasoning performance in RL with verifiable rewards.
items.why: Global entropy metrics can mislead when diagnosing RLVR training, so reward-conditioned diagnostics may give engineers more reliable training signals.

items.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
items.summary: A paper studies recovering readable skill documents from LoRA adapters by writing text back from adapter weights and a frozen base model, scored by instruction coverage and task success.
items.why: Compiled LoRA skills lose editability and auditability, so recovering their source text could help teams inspect and move agent skills across models.

items.title: FusionCLIP: Multimodal Contrastive Pretraining for Fusion Plasma Diagnostics
items.summary: FusionCLIP is a multimodal contrastive pretraining method that aligns visible-light tokamak videos with multivariate diagnostic signals for fusion plasma diagnostics.

items.title: Mosaic:montage-agnostic self-distilled graph learning for subject-independent ieeg seizure detection
items.summary: Researchers introduce MOSAIC, a lightweight graph-learning framework for subject-independent intracranial EEG seizure detection that handles varying electrode montages across patients.
items.why: Handling variable channel counts and montages without per-patient tuning could make medical time-series models more deployable across patients.

items.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
items.summary: Researchers propose e-means, an exponential moving average variant of mini-batch k-means that reportedly outperforms standard k-means in one-tenth the epochs, with scaling laws for its hyperparameters.
items.why: A faster, hyperparameter-light clustering method could cut compute for data curation, retrieval and quantization pipelines.

items.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
items.summary: Researchers present BEiTScore++, an uncertainty-aware reference-free image captioning metric that outputs conformally calibrated confidence intervals alongside alignment scores.
items.why: Calibrated confidence intervals make automated captioning evaluation more trustworthy when deployed under input ambiguity and domain shift.

items.title: V-STORM: A Structure-Aware Grounded Chain of Thought Dataset for Faithful and Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Video Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce V-STORM, a structure-aware framework and dataset that links chain-of-thought reasoning steps to explicit spatio-temporal evidence in videos for multimodal LLM training.
items.why: Verifiable step-level grounding data may help teams train and evaluate video reasoning models that cite where evidence appears.

items.title: Active Learning of Robust Models
items.summary: A paper studies active learning for training robust models that must handle data distribution shifts between training and deployment while minimizing labeling costs.

items.title: Multimodal Training with Knowledge Traction for Video Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose a weakly supervised video anomaly detection method that injects LLM-generated textual prior knowledge via dictionary learning during training.
items.why: Using external textual priors in training may improve anomaly detectors' robustness and generalization for video monitoring systems.

items.title: Query-Guided RoPE Modulation for Lost-in-the-Middle Mitigation in Long-Context LLMs
items.summary: Researchers propose QGPM, a query-guided RoPE modulation method that remaps positions per query to mitigate the lost-in-the-middle problem in long-context language models.
items.why: Query-aware positional adjustments target a known long-context failure mode that affects retrieval-heavy applications.

items.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), which uses gradient updates at test time to encode memory in world models for long-term planning tasks.

items.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
items.summary: Researchers introduce LambdaMix, a parameter-efficient method that trains one low-rank adapter per objective so a single frozen model can be steered across preference trade-offs.
items.why: Preference-conditioned adapters could let teams tune trade-offs between objectives at inference without training separate models.

items.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
items.summary: Researchers show gradient inversion attacks can reconstruct private client data from federated fine-tuning of LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers, challenging assumptions about PEFT privacy.
items.why: Teams using federated learning with LoRA should not assume parameter-efficient updates protect client data from server-side reconstruction.

items.title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity and Semantics
items.summary: Researchers propose RelGuard, a differentially private framework for GraphRAG designed to protect entity connectivity and relationship semantics against knowledge graph reconstruction via black-box access.
items.why: GraphRAG deployments exposing query access may leak knowledge graph structure, and this offers formal privacy guarantees against that.

items.title: How Much Conversation History Does an AI Agent Need?
items.summary: A study on 1,100 BEAM questions finds benchmark scores generally rise with larger conversation-history passage budgets, with diminishing gains per additional token at higher budgets.
items.why: Results quantify the cost-versus-accuracy trade-off when choosing how much conversation history to pass an agent.

items.title: Goodhart in the Planner: Sampling-Based Control Exploits Rewards Learned from Human Preferences
items.summary: The paper shows that sampling-based planners optimizing learned human-preference reward models can degrade true task return, with harder search cutting return by up to 76% in tests.
items.why: Stronger search against a learned reward model can exploit its errors, so teams using best-of-N or MPC should validate against true objectives.

items.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose SURE, a spatiotemporal uncertainty representation for vision-language-action policies that avoids exact pointwise action targets to improve learning efficiency from demonstrations.
items.why: Reducing dependence on large demonstration volumes could lower data costs for training robot control policies.

items.title: Verifier Noise Is a Temperature: Testing Tilt Predictions in Finite-Budget LLM-Guided Search
items.summary: A theoretical study tests whether verifier noise acts as a temperature in LLM-guided keep-if-better search, predicting the stationary distribution is the mutation equilibrium tilted by exp(beta f).

items.title: Empirical Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in SSH Infrastructure
items.summary: A study scans SSH fingerprint data from 1.52 million hosts to measure real-world adoption of post-quantum cryptography in SSH infrastructure.
items.why: It shows how far PQC has actually reached in deployed SSH servers, informing migration planning for teams securing remote access.

items.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
items.summary: ICare-DT is a Transformer-based digital twin that updates intensive care patient forecasts hourly from new measurements without retraining, tested on eICU-CRD data.
items.why: It shows a method for continuously updating clinical forecasts from routine records without retraining models, a pattern relevant to healthcare ML systems.

items.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
items.summary: MemoryDojo is a benchmark that measures how malicious instructions poisoning LLM agent memory propagate across different memory architectures.
items.why: Agent memory is an attack surface, and the benchmark helps teams compare how different memory designs resist poisoning before deployment.

items.title: Safety Is $\Pi_1$, Provability Is $\Sigma_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
items.summary: A paper reads a claimed OpenAI agent breach of Hugging Face and OpenAI's AI-generated math proofs through one theoretical framework.
items.why: The text is a theoretical essay built on claimed events with dates in the future relative to its arXiv ID, offering little concrete engineering guidance.

items.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
items.summary: Controlled experiments in the LURK Werewolf game test how linguistic complexity and politeness in messages change how LLM agents judge and act.
items.why: Phrasing of inter-agent messages can shift other agents' behavior, which matters for designing multi-agent communication protocols.

items.title: ROSE: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: ROSE proposes a risk-aware orthogonal subspace method for lifelong knowledge editing in multimodal LLMs to reduce forgetting during sequential edits.
items.why: Sequential factual edits to multimodal models can erode prior capabilities, so this approach targets a practical maintenance problem for deployed MLLMs.

items.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
items.summary: The paper frames stale repository instruction files like AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as documentation debt that adds cost to every later coding-agent session.
items.why: Outdated agent config files can silently raise per-session costs for coding agents, so teams should treat them as maintained artifacts.

items.title: Scaling Graph Similarity Learning with Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: A paper proposes scaling graph similarity learning with graph neural networks to approximate NP-hard Graph Edit Distance and Maximum Common Subgraph computations.
items.why: Learned approximations could make graph similarity tasks in chemistry and program analysis tractable at larger scale.

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate automated AI-driven discovery of formally verified quantum programs beyond small instances that classical computers can evaluate.
items.why: LLM-driven discovery loops are being applied to quantum algorithms, a direction that could shorten algorithm development cycles.

items.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Grasp-TAGS uses critic distillation to select task-aware grasps for prehensile loco-manipulation by mobile manipulators.

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.summary: GRAC proposes graph-based retrieval-augmented captioning that represents surgical scenes as graphs to generate automated surgical scene descriptions.
items.why: Automated structured scene descriptions could reduce manual review of surgical records, a use case for clinical documentation tooling.

items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.summary: The paper reports that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist VLA and world-action policies, introducing the AMP1 harness.
items.why: Generalist models commanding robots directly may outperform trained specialist policies, a shift in how robotics stacks could be architected.

items.title: L-MARS: Legal Multi-Agent System with Agentic Search and Citation-Faithfulness Audit
items.summary: L-MARS is an open multi-agent legal QA system that audits each claim against its cited source using a six-class taxonomy and strict-ALCE scoring.
items.why: Citation-faithfulness auditing shows how to verify grounded claims in LLM answers, relevant to any high-stakes RAG application.

items.title: Sentinel Agents for Secure and Trustworthy Agentic AI in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Sentinel Agents proposes a security layer that monitors inter-agent messages using rule-based, behavioral, and LLM-based checks, with a Coordinator enforcing policy.
items.why: Propagation of a single adversarial message across agents is a real risk, and this architecture offers a concrete monitoring pattern for multi-agent systems.

items.title: Limit Analysis for Symbolic Multi-step Reasoning Tasks with Information Propagation Rules Based on Transformers
items.summary: A theoretical paper derives limits on the number of symbolic reasoning steps a multi-layer Transformer can perform in a single pass.
items.why: It gives formal bounds on single-pass reasoning depth tied to attention layer count, which informs expectations about model reasoning limits.

items.title: Comparing Explanations is Not Enough, Explain the Change: New Standards are Needed to Explain Behavioral Shifts in Large Language Models
items.summary: An arXiv paper argues that current explainability methods cannot explain behavioral shifts in large language models, and calls for new standards to explain the change between model versions.
items.why: Engineers retraining or fine-tuning models need ways to explain behavior changes between checkpoints, not just compare separate explanations.

items.title: OMG-Agent: Toward Robust Missing Modality Generation with Decoupled Coarse-to-Fine Agentic Workflows
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes OMG-Agent, a coarse-to-fine agentic workflow for generating missing modalities in multimodal data, aiming to reduce hallucination and retrieval rigidity.

items.title: Approximating the Reachability Value of Posterior-Deterministic POMDPs
items.summary: An arXiv paper shows that the maximal probability of reaching a target set of states can be approximated to arbitrary precision for posterior-deterministic POMDPs.

items.title: Counterfactual Distillation: Internalizing Reflective Experience into LLM Agent
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes Counterfactual Distillation, a method for internalizing reflective interaction experience into LLM agents to address sparse feedback in long-horizon tasks.
items.why: Offers a training approach for agents that learn from heterogeneous interaction feedback beyond outcome-only reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

items.title: EvoAgent: An Evolvable Agent Framework with Skill Learning and Multi-Agent Delegation
items.summary: An arXiv paper presents EvoAgent, an evolvable LLM agent framework combining structured skill learning, user-feedback-driven evolution, and hierarchical sub-agent delegation.

items.title: ClawTrace: Cost-Aware Tracing for LLM Agent Skill Distillation
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces ClawTrace, which records cost-attributed agent traces per step, and CostCraft, which uses them to write rules for distilled agent skills.
items.why: Per-step cost attribution could help teams tune agent pipelines so they remove expensive steps that do not affect outcomes.

items.title: Taming the Centaur(s) with LAPITHS: a framework for a theoretically grounded interpretation of AI performances
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces LAPITHS, a framework arguing that claims made about the CENTAUR model as a unified model of cognition are not theoretically or empirically justified.

items.title: TimeTok: Granularity-Controllable Time-Series Generation via Hierarchical Tokenization
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces TimeTok, a hierarchical tokenization framework for time-series generation that lets users control the temporal granularity of inputs and outputs.

items.title: Intentmaking and Sensemaking: Human Interaction with AI-Guided Mathematical Discovery
items.summary: An arXiv study of 11 expert mathematicians using the AlphaEvolve coding agent over more than 2,300 experiments examines the human-AI loop in mathematical discovery.
items.why: Shows where human judgment bottlenecks AI-driven discovery, relevant to designing human-in-the-loop research agent tools.

items.title: Self-Programmed Execution for Language-Model Agents
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces self-programmed execution, in which the model completion itself acts as the orchestrator program for language model agents instead of a fixed harness.
items.why: Proposes moving agent orchestration logic from the harness into the model, which could change how agent systems are architected.

items.title: Embeddings for Preferences, Not Semantics
items.summary: An arXiv paper argues that standard text embeddings measure semantic similarity, while collective decision-making and facility location need a preferential similarity measure.
items.why: Teams building embedding-based collective decision or clustering tools may need preference-aware embeddings rather than standard semantic ones.

items.title: Agentic AI Scientists Are Not Built For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
items.summary: A position paper argues that agentic AI scientists, though useful as co-scientists, are not yet built for autonomous scientific discovery, citing problem selection and missing lab knowledge.

items.title: NeuroMAS: Multi-Agent Systems as Neural Networks with Joint Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes NeuroMAS, which treats a multi-agent language system as a trainable neural-network-like architecture with hidden textual signals and joint reinforcement learning.

items.title: Learning to Solve Compositional Geometry Routing Problems
items.summary: An arXiv paper studies the Compositional Geometry Routing Problem, a superclass of routing problems covering point, line, area, and hybrid task geometries, and proposes learning-based solutions.

items.title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes Gated DeltaNet-2, which decouples the erase and write gates in linear attention so that memory editing does not scramble existing associations.
items.why: Better-controlled memory updates in linear attention could improve long-context efficiency for model architects working on constant-memory decoding.

items.title: SuiChat-CN: Benchmarking Contextual Suicide Risk Assessment in Chinese Group Chats
items.summary: Researchers introduced SuiChat-CN, a benchmark for assessing contextual suicide risk in Chinese group chats on instant messaging platforms.
items.why: Shows that multi-party, implicit chat messages need context-aware safety evaluation beyond the post-level analysis common in existing risk detection tools.

items.title: WorldCoder-Bench: Benchmarking Physically Grounded 3D World Synthesis
items.summary: WorldCoder-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can generate executable, physically grounded 3D worlds in browser-native Three.js.
items.why: Gives teams a way to test LLM-generated interactive 3D code against runtime state and physical constraints, not just pixels or DOM output.

items.title: Uncertainty Aware Functional Behavior Prediction and Material Fatigue Assessment for Circular Factory
items.summary: The paper proposes uncertainty-aware functional behavior prediction and material fatigue assessment to decide reuse of returned products in circular factories.
items.why: Links component fatigue to system-level functional prognosis, which could inform reuse decisions for returned industrial products.

items.title: From Senses to Decisions: The Information Flow of Auditory and Visual Perception in Multimodal LLMs
items.summary: A study traces how audio and visual signals flow through the internal layers of audio-visual multimodal LLMs to shape their answers.
items.why: Interpretability findings on modality routing can guide debugging and design of multimodal models that process audio and video.

items.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?
items.summary: The paper defines Agentic Abstention, the problem of deciding when LLM agents should stop taking tool-using actions under uncertainty instead of continuing.
items.why: Agents that keep calling tools on underspecified or unachievable goals waste cost and time, so stop-decision reliability matters for production agent design.

items.title: Coachable Agents for Interactive Gameplay
items.summary: The paper presents coachable agents for interactive gameplay, which learn behaviors that can be adjusted through user guidance rather than a single near-optimal policy.

items.title: EVOQUANT: Self-Evolving Verifier-Guided Strategy Optimization for Robust Quantitative Trading
items.summary: EVOQUANT is a framework where LLMs diagnose and revise quantitative trading strategies under verifier guidance to limit hallucinated edits and backtest overfitting.
items.why: Shows a verifier-in-the-loop pattern for constraining LLM code and strategy edits in high-stakes domains where overfitting is a risk.

items.title: GABench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Graph Analysis Tasks
items.summary: GABench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on graph analysis tasks, covering a broader range of graph tasks and graph types than prior benchmarks.
items.why: Provides a more comprehensive testbed for agentic data-access and multi-step operations over graph environments.

items.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
items.summary: RST is a recursive framework that synthesizes verified long-horizon terminal tasks for training terminal agents, extending seed tasks while realigning instructions and verifiers.
items.why: Offers a route to scale high-quality long-horizon agent training data without relying on costly manual authoring or unverified LLM generation.

items.title: Improving Generalization Robustness of Multimodal RLVR
items.summary: The paper diagnoses why RLVR gains in multimodal LLMs are brittle to paraphrasing and prompt changes, and proposes fixes to the training objective.
items.why: Highlights that reward design and training distribution coverage can make multimodal gains fragile, a concern for high-stakes deployments such as medical VQA.

items.title: Who Speaks Matters: Authority-Aware Multi-View RAG over Italian Parliamentary Proceedings
items.summary: ParliamentRAG is an authority-aware multi-view RAG system over Italian Chamber of Deputies transcripts, addressing speaker dominance and citation misattribution.
items.why: Demonstrates retrieval design choices, such as weighting by speaker expertise, that reduce citation errors in politically sensitive corpora.

items.title: TailSieve: Partial-Rollout-Guided Tail Routing for LLM Rollouts
items.summary: TailSieve is a partial-rollout-guided routing method that reduces the impact of long-tail generations on synchronous LLM rollouts.
items.why: Long-tail generations can stall entire RL post-training or evaluation steps, so better routing directly improves rollout throughput.

items.title: Agentic AI uncovers conserved cross-tissue protein co-abundance programs inaccessible to single-dataset analysis
items.summary: An agentic AI system identified protein co-abundance programs conserved across tissues, going beyond single-dataset and pre-selected tissue-pair analyses.
items.why: Shows agentic pipelines can systematically assess thousands of candidate clusters across heterogeneous evidence at a scale manual curation cannot reach.

items.title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: AgentGrad proposes intervention-guided prompt optimization for multi-agent systems, addressing limits in how textual gradients are extracted and aggregated.
items.why: Targets the prompt-tuning step in multi-agent systems, where per-agent prompt quality drives overall performance.

items.title: LLMs as Post-hoc Auditors of Physiological Plausibility in Symbolic Regression: A Clinician-Evaluated Case Study
items.summary: A clinician-evaluated case study tests whether LLMs can audit symbolic regression equations for physiological plausibility after they are generated.
items.why: Suggests LLMs may serve as post-hoc plausibility checks on interpretable models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: MoMHa: Multi-Objective Optimization of LLM Harnesses over Accuracy, Safety, and Tokens
items.summary: MoMHa proposes Meta-Harness, which treats LLM harness design as a multi-objective search over accuracy, behavioural safety, and token cost.
items.why: Harness design choices can trade accuracy against safety and token use, so engineers should evaluate harnesses on more than accuracy alone.

items.title: Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas
items.summary: A paper extends program-of-layers (PoLar) by treating LLM layers as a library of functions, enabling input-dependent routing that reportedly improves on fixed-depth forward passes.
items.why: Dynamic layer routing could offer adaptive compute per input, but the summary gives too little detail on results to assess practical value.

items.title: Structured Sparse Memory for Recurrent Reasoning
items.summary: CHARM is a compact hybrid recurrent model for ARC-style reasoning that combines structured task memory, synthetic augmentation data, and inference-time aggregation.
items.why: Small recurrent models with structured memory are becoming competitive on abstract reasoning benchmarks, a possible alternative to large models for narrow tasks.

items.title: Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers test the Jev judgment model, which outputs option probabilities in one call, on reasoning, games, and robot control, finding it reliable only when the answer is judgeable from the input.
items.why: Single-call judgment models can serve as agent action selectors, but engineers need to know they fail on decisions requiring simulation rather than evaluation.

items.title: Continual Graph Memory and Community Infrastructure for AI-Assisted Mathematical Discovery
items.summary: Ansatz, a research harness with continual graph memory, and Ansatze, a community platform, are presented for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, reporting results on First Proof batches.
items.why: The paper describes graph-based memory for multi-step AI research workflows, though its reported outcomes are model-assessed and limited in scope.

items.title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
items.summary: HarnessNet proposes hierarchical joint evolution of harnesses across multi-agent systems, using feedback without sharing agent internals or foundation model weights.
items.why: Multi-agent systems need scalable harness optimization that respects access restrictions between agents, which matters for production agent architectures.

items.title: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate
items.summary: AuthGateBench is a policy-guided benchmark evaluating LLMs as authorization gates for coding agents, targeting failures like scope escalation beyond user-granted permissions.
items.why: Automated approval of agent actions by LLM classifiers can permit out-of-scope actions, so teams deploying such gates need this kind of testing.

items.title: SteadyThought: Mitigating LLM Under-Thinking via Thought-Level Preference Optimization
items.summary: SteadyThought proposes a thought-level preference optimization method to reduce under-thinking, where reasoning models switch thoughts excessively without sustaining promising lines.
items.why: Reducing premature reasoning switches could improve accuracy of reasoning models without over-suppressing useful exploration.

items.title: CoRS: Fast Neural Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling via Composite Interval State Reuse
items.summary: CoRS speeds up neural flexible job-shop scheduling by reusing interval-level graph representations across several decisions while updating feasibility after each action.
items.why: The two-timescale approach could cut inference cost for learned scheduling solvers in industrial optimization, though gains are not quantified in the summary.

items.title: REFLEX: RNA Ensemble Generation via Flexibility-Calibrated Stochastic Bridge
items.summary: REFLEX is a sequence-conditioned generator of RNA conformational ensembles that uses experimental B-factors to calibrate flexibility in a stochastic bridge model.
items.why: The text is a scientific method for molecular biology and offers little direct relevance to most engineering or tech leadership work.

items.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
items.summary: HarnessMinusMinus technical report consolidates work on reducing agent harness token overhead through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement across coding and visual-agent settings.
items.why: Skipping redundant model reasoning after tool results could meaningfully lower token costs for agent deployments.

items.title: DecoyCount: Evaluating Visual-Reasoning Misalignment in Counting
items.summary: DecoyCount is a benchmark of 1,586 images with decoys that separates perception from reasoning failures in vision-language model counting tasks.
items.why: Showing that counting errors stem partly from visual misalignment helps teams diagnose whether VLM failures come from perception or reasoning.

items.title: Radial Kernel Attention for Global Feature Exchange in Polymer Machine Learning Force Fields
items.summary: Radial Kernel Attention is introduced for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields, aiming to avoid local neighbor graphs and quadratic all-pair attention costs.
items.why: The method targets scientific force-field modeling and offers limited direct relevance to most engineering teams.

items.title: A Discrete-Time Variational Objective for Degenerate Diffusion and Equivalence to Flow Matching
items.summary: A paper proposes a discrete-time variational objective for deterministic-generator diffusion models and shows formal equivalence between these degenerate diffusion models and flow matching.
items.why: The theoretical link between degenerate diffusion and flow matching gives a unified view, though it has little immediate practical implication.

items.title: Seeing What Matters, Verifying What Pays: Load-Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Uni-LaSpec is a block-parallel speculative decoding method for vision-language models that conditions drafts on relevant image regions and adapts verification to GPU load.
items.why: Load-adaptive verification and selective visual conditioning could speed up VLM serving without changing output distributions.

items.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduced LUCA, a configurable synthetic world that evaluates agents' experimental reasoning under known ground truth, separately scoring experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention.
items.why: It offers a way to test whether agents succeed for the right reasons rather than judging only final outcomes.

items.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
items.summary: Researchers released AceAction-5M, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games, organized around complete tasks with hierarchical subgoals for vision-language-action learning.
items.why: Game gameplay data with hierarchical task labels may help teams train action models more cheaply than physical-world data.

items.title: Treating the Symptom, Missing the Cause: Anatomy of a Scientific Reasoning Failure
items.summary: A study of controlled synthetic regulatory systems found that seven LLMs restore healthy phenotypes more often than they identify the underlying hidden fault.
items.why: It shows agents can appear successful by treating symptoms, which matters for evaluating scientific or debugging agents.

items.title: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
items.summary: Researchers propose a formal definition of catastrophic performance for misspecified AI objectives, based on baseline and orthogonal reference values.
items.why: It gives a rigorous way to separate merely suboptimal objectives from catastrophic ones in misalignment risk analysis.

items.title: AdaFloor: Adaptive Floor Planning and Rank-Time Reuse for Long-Tail MoE RL Rollouts
items.summary: AdaFloor proposes adaptive floor planning and rank-time reuse to reduce idle accelerator time during long-tail MoE reinforcement-learning rollouts.
items.why: Idle rank-time in expert-parallel rollouts is a concrete efficiency loss for teams running MoE RL post-training.

items.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone
items.summary: Researchers introduced BabyTheorist, a benchmark for learning reusable theories from pure visual observations and applying them to new situations.

items.title: Stay on the Manifold: Hierarchical Bayesian Trajectory-Family Transfer for Sparse-Target Reconstruction and Sampling
items.summary: Researchers propose hierarchical Bayesian trajectory principal-manifold sampling to reconstruct and sample trajectories from sparse target observations using learned source trajectory families.

items.title: Differentiable Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Researchers introduce sequential barrier quadratic programming, a method for computing parametric solution sensitivities of nonlinear programs for differentiable nonlinear model predictive control.
items.why: Efficient solution sensitivities enable combining learning algorithms with nonlinear MPC in control systems.

items.title: Equivariant Spherical Transformer for Efficient Molecular Modeling
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Equivariant Spherical Transformer, a plug-and-play module that adds Transformer attention to spherical representations for 3D molecular modeling.
items.why: It offers a drop-in module that may improve expressiveness of equivariant graph networks for molecular tasks.

items.title: From Images to Signals: Are Large Vision Models Useful for Time Series Analysis?
items.summary: A study tests whether large vision models are useful for time series analysis, presenting what it calls the first principled investigation of this question.
items.why: Results indicate whether teams should adopt vision foundation models for time series tasks or stick with other approaches.

items.title: BNPO: Beta Normalization Policy Optimization
items.summary: Researchers propose BNPO, a policy optimization method using adaptive Beta-based reward normalization to address instability from static normalization in binary-reward LLM reinforcement learning.
items.why: Adaptive reward normalization targets unstable gradients in RL training for LLM reasoning, a practical training concern.

items.title: Subjective Experience in AI Systems: What Do AI Researchers and the Public Believe?
items.summary: A survey of 582 AI researchers and 825 US adults finds both groups think AI systems are unlikely to have subjective experience now but expect it may become more likely.

items.title: AblationBench: Evaluating Automated Planning of Ablations in Empirical AI Research
items.summary: Researchers introduce AblationBench, a benchmark of 83-plus instances testing agents on planning ablation experiments for empirical AI research, covering author and reviewer tasks.
items.why: It measures whether research agents can plan the ablations that substantiate scientific claims.

items.title: End-to-End On-Device Quantization-Aware Training for LLMs at Inference Cost
items.summary: Researchers propose ZeroQAT, a zeroth-order quantization-aware training framework for LLMs that uses forward-only gradient estimation to avoid backpropagation and reduce memory use.
items.why: Forward-only quantization-aware training could let teams fine-tune low-bit LLMs with much lower memory cost.

items.title: Align Your Query: Representation Alignment for Multimodality Medical Object Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose aligning DETR-style object queries with modality context so one medical detector can train across CXR, CT, and MRI data.

items.title: Enhancing Neural Code Representation with Additional Context
items.summary: An empirical study tests whether adding context like version history or structural relationships to code representations improves four software engineering tasks.
items.why: Suggests richer code context beyond source alone may improve clone detection, summarisation, and vulnerability detection models.

items.title: ReefNet: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Fine-Grained Coral Reef Recognition
items.summary: Researchers released ReefNet, a public coral reef dataset with 479,027 expert-audited annotations across 39 taxonomic labels for fine-grained recognition.
items.why: Provides a large, taxonomy-aligned benchmark for visual recognition of similar taxa in heterogeneous underwater survey imagery.

items.title: AURA: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for AI-Driven Adaptive Conversational Surveys
items.summary: AURA, a reinforcement learning framework, is proposed to let AI survey chatbots adapt within a session instead of relying on fixed dialogue trees.
items.why: Shows RL-driven adaptive dialogue as an alternative to static prompt templates for conversational data collection products.

items.title: Physics Steering: Causal Control of Cross-Domain Concepts in a Physics Foundation Model
items.summary: Researchers show that Walrus, a physics foundation model, has linear directions in its activations that enable causal steering of cross-domain physics concepts.
items.why: Extends activation steering from language and vision models to scientific foundation models, relevant to interpretability and control work.

items.title: Predicting Public Health Impacts of Electricity Usage
items.summary: HealthPredictor, a domain-specific AI model, links electricity use to public health outcomes through an end-to-end pipeline.
items.why: Offers a demand-side tool for health-informed energy management, relevant mainly to energy and public health stakeholders.

items.title: Limitations of Using Identical Distributions for Training and Testing When Learning Boolean Functions
items.summary: A theoretical study examines when training on a distribution different from the test distribution helps generalization for learning Boolean functions, allowing optimal algorithm choice per distribution.

items.title: Evolutionary Architecture Search through Grammar-Based Sequence Alignment
items.summary: Researchers introduce two adapted Smith-Waterman variants to compute edit distance in a grammar-based evolutionary neural architecture search.
items.why: Offers a method for reusing architecture components in expressive NAS search spaces, which may aid automated model design.

items.title: Outgrowing the Curse of Multilinguality: Scaling Strategies for Efficient Language Adaptation
items.summary: A study investigates whether upscaling English base models is a more efficient way than massively multilingual training to adapt models to new target languages.
items.why: Compares compute-matched scaling strategies for language adaptation, informing how teams build models for medium- and lower-resource languages.

items.title: MCGI: Manifold-Consistent Graph Indexing for Billion-Scale Disk-Resident Vector Search
items.summary: MCGI, a disk-resident graph indexing method, uses local intrinsic dimensionality to allocate search effort for billion-scale approximate nearest neighbor vector search.
items.why: Targets performance loss in high-dimensional graph-based vector search, relevant to teams running large-scale retrieval on disk.

items.title: Remote Sensing Change Detection via Weak Temporal Supervision
items.summary: A weak temporal supervision strategy is introduced for semantic change detection in remote sensing, aiming to reduce reliance on costly pixel-level annotations.

items.title: Outcome-Based RL Provably Leads Transformers to Reason, but Only With the Right Data
items.summary: A theoretical analysis of single-layer linear Transformers shows that outcome-based RL can lead to chain-of-thought reasoning, but only with appropriate training data.
items.why: Gives a theoretical account of when sparse outcome rewards induce reasoning, relevant to designing RL training for reasoning models.

items.title: Fast Statistical Rates for Flow Matching without Curvature Assumptions
items.summary: A paper proves fast statistical sample-complexity rates for flow matching in Wasserstein distance without curvature assumptions, under exact empirical risk minimization.
items.why: Provides theoretical guarantees for flow-based generative models, though results assume exact risk minimization over a fixed network class.

items.title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: MemSkill proposes learnable, evolvable memory skills for LLM agents, replacing static hand-designed operations for extracting and revising memory.
items.why: Points toward agent memory systems that adapt their own memory routines instead of relying on fixed procedures for long interaction histories.

items.summary: Nvidia's board is launching an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, reportedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on the company.
items.why: A governance probe at a core AI chip supplier, tied to alleged espionage, could affect supply chains, partner trust, and export-compliance risk.

items.title: How I Fight AI Brain Fry
items.summary: A Hacker News post shares a blog article on ways to fight "AI brain fry," the mental fatigue from heavy AI tool use.

items.title: Apple is racing to make Siri more agentic
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Apple CEO John Ternus is pressing AI chief Craig Federighi to speed up Siri's roadmap and ship a powerful AI agent to compete with rivals.
items.why: Apple's push toward agentic Siri signals how major platforms will expose AI agents to users and third-party developers.

items.title: Silicon Valley Promises AI Will Cure Disease. Drugmaker CEOs Aren't Buying It
items.summary: A WSJ article reports that drugmaker CEOs are skeptical of Silicon Valley claims that AI will cure disease.

items.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
items.summary: Rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some Eminem hits are suing Suno, alleging it generates music and lyrics mimicking those artists.
items.why: Another lawsuit against Suno adds to legal pressure on generative music models over training data and voice or style imitation.

items.summary: TechCrunch's Equity podcast discussed what the midterm elections mean for Elon Musk and the tech industry, including data centers.

items.title: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
items.summary: A Verge reviewer tested NYT Cooking's AI assistant for weeknight dinner, finding it helped with chicken but caused problems with a cake.
items.why: This is a consumer product review with little relevance to engineering or technology leadership decisions.

items.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
items.summary: According to The New York Times, the US approved New Matrix, a Chinese firm with an empty office, to handle Nvidia H200 AI chip sales.
items.why: It raises questions about how export-control vetting of Chinese buyers of advanced AI chips is being carried out.
